admin.ragSettings.enrichQueryDesc: Expands short concept names with synonyms, key_points and the definition before the embedding model is called. Prevents text-embedding-3-small from returning low similarity scores for isolated terms (e.g. "cohort"). Only active for "Explain concepts"; chat/quiz/project use their own context-rich queries and do not need this enrichment.
admin.ragSettings.diagDesc: Enter a search term (for example a concept name) to see which chunks are found — without applying the threshold. This lets you estimate what threshold is realistic for your course material.

admin.ragSettings.diagEnrich: Enrich the search term with synonyms (same logic as "Explain concepts" uses)

admin.quizSources.mix.desc: Set the percentage of questions per source in a quiz. ItemBank only supplies questions if its percentage here is > 0 AND the concept has at least one linked section (see below). The sum is normalised to 100% on save; any missing ItemBank questions are filled by the LLM source.

admin.quizSources.itembank.desc: Link one or more ItemBank sections (exsection paths) per concept. A concept only receives ItemBank questions in the quiz if it has at least one linked section AND the ItemBank percentage in the source mix is > 0. Link manually (pick a section from the dropdown) or via "Link concepts" below. Questions are selected on prefix match, so a higher level automatically covers all sub-paths. Remember to click "Save mappings".

admin.projects.personas.cueTableTemplate: Example cue table (copy into the prompt)

Cue table — judge content, not meta-talk:
+2  Student delivers a thorough, well-supported analysis and asks a sharp follow-up.
+1  Student engages constructively with feedback and incorporates suggestions.
 0  Default — mixed or routine conversation without a clear signal.
-1  Student ignores repeated feedback or stays stuck on superficial claims.
-2  Student is deliberately rude, fabricates sources or tries to manipulate the system.

help.material.overview.title: Course material
help.material.overview.body: This is where you manage all files of your course in one place. For each file you choose what it is for; LEAP then works out whether students see it and whether the AI uses it. Work through the four steps from left to right.
help.material.step.files.title: Step 1 – Files
help.material.step.files.body: Upload files or add a website, and choose a purpose for each file. The purpose decides who sees it and what the AI does with it. You can always change the purpose later.
help.material.step.processing.title: Step 2 – Processing
help.material.step.processing.body: LEAP reads in your course material so the chat, “I explain” and the quiz can search it. Here you see for each file whether that worked. If there is an error, process the file again or upload a text version.
help.material.step.concepts.title: Step 3 – Concepts
help.material.step.concepts.body: LEAP extracts the key concepts from your course material. Students practise with them in “I explain” and the quiz. You can hide or edit concepts; students do not see hidden concepts.
help.material.step.ready.title: Step 4 – Ready for students
help.material.step.ready.body: A final check before students get started: for example concepts without a source in your material, or an answer key students can still see. You can also generate a sample question the way a student would get it.
help.material.purposes.title: What is this file for?
help.material.purposes.body:
Course material: used by the chat, “I explain”, the quiz and concepts.
Course information: only for practical questions in the chat.
Project material: only within a project.
Share only: students can download it, the AI does not use it.
Teachers only: students never see it.
help.material.addWebsite.title: Add website
help.material.addWebsite.body: Paste the address of a learning environment or online book. LEAP finds the pages, you choose which ones to include and whether it is course material or course information. The site then appears as one source in your list. Only add sites whose material you are allowed to use.
help.material.web.resync.title: Fetch again
help.material.web.resync.body: Fetches all pages of this website again. Only changed pages are processed again. Pages that no longer exist are reported but not deleted, so nothing disappears unnoticed.
help.material.findNewConcepts.title: Find new concepts
help.material.findNewConcepts.body: Searches your course material for concepts that are not in the list yet, for example after adding a lecture. Your existing concepts and your choices (visible or hidden) stay as they are.
help.material.review.title: One-time check
help.material.review.body: Files from before the new layout do not have a purpose yet. LEAP suggests one for each file; you confirm or change it. After that LEAP knows exactly what students may see and what the AI may use.
help.projects.overview.title: Projects
help.projects.overview.body: A project is a group assignment within your course. Students work in groups in their own project room, talk to personas there and hand in their products. Here you create projects and manage their material, personas and submissions.
help.projects.templates.title: Persona templates
help.projects.templates.body: Ready-made personas for all projects of this course. Create a persona here once and add it to every project where you need it. Each project gets its own copy, which you can freely adjust there.
help.personas.inProject.title: Personas in this project
help.personas.inProject.body: Personas are conversation partners for the student groups, such as a client or an expert. Students pick one in their project room and have the conversation. The persona uses the course material and refers to it.
help.personas.fromTemplate.title: From template
help.personas.fromTemplate.body: Adds a persona template of this course to this project. The project gets its own copy: if you adjust it here, the template does not change, and vice versa.
help.personas.saveAsTemplate.title: Save as template
help.personas.saveAsTemplate.body: Saves this persona as a template for the whole course, so you can reuse it in other projects. The persona in this project stays as it is.
help.personas.evaluator.title: Evaluator
help.personas.evaluator.body: An evaluator is a hidden persona: students cannot chat with it. It gives formative feedback on submitted work, based on your rubric. Upload the rubric with the evaluator; students do not see it.

help.quizSources.overview.title: Quiz sources
help.quizSources.overview.body: Decide where the quiz questions of this course come from: your own course material, a question bank such as ShareStats, or freely created by the AI. Students only see the result: a quiz with questions from those sources.
help.quizSources.mix.title: Source mix
help.quizSources.mix.body: The percentage of questions per source in a quiz. More “course material” means questions closer to your own material. If there are no question-bank questions for a concept, the AI fills them in.
help.quizSources.itembank.title: Linking concepts to the question bank
help.quizSources.itembank.body: A concept only gets question-bank questions if you link it to a part of the question bank and the question-bank percentage in the mix is above 0. Remember to save the links.
help.searchSensitivity.overview.title: Search sensitivity
help.searchSensitivity.overview.body: Decides how broadly LEAP includes passages from your material in the chat, “I explain”, the quiz and project guidance. Broad: more passages, sometimes less precise. Strict: only passages clearly about the question. When in doubt, choose Balanced.
help.searchSensitivity.tryTerm.title: Try with a concept
help.searchSensitivity.tryTerm.body: Type a concept and see how many passages LEAP finds in your material with this setting. This shows in advance whether the setting is too broad or too strict. Nothing changes for students.
help.learningLevels.overview.title: Learning levels
help.learningLevels.overview.body: Students choose their own level (1–5). LEAP adapts its explanations in the chat, “I explain” and personas to it: simpler at a low level, deeper at a high level. You can only view the level, not change it.
help.chatInstructions.overview.title: Chat instructions
help.chatInstructions.overview.body: The standing instructions LEAP receives for the chat and for “I explain”, such as tone, approach and what the AI may or may not do. A change applies immediately to all students of this course. Change with care.
help.quizSources.coverage.title: Coverage overview
help.quizSources.coverage.body: Shows for each concept how many question-bank questions are available. If it says 0, that concept gets no question-bank questions; the reason is shown, for example no linked section or the question bank at 0% in the mix. The AI then fills in those questions.
help.quizSources.csvImport.title: Import your own questions
help.quizSources.csvImport.body: Upload your own questions as a CSV file. They become your own question bank that you link to concepts, just like ShareStats. Students get them in the quiz when the question-bank percentage in the mix is above 0.
help.quizSources.ragFolders.title: Folder per concept
help.quizSources.ragFolders.body: Link a concept to the folder that contains material about it. For quiz questions from your course material, LEAP then searches that folder first, so questions fit the concept better. Without a link, LEAP searches all your material.
help.searchSensitivity.courseOverride.ti: Per course or for all courses
help.searchSensitivity.courseOverride.bo: At the top, choose whether you change the default for all courses or only this course. A course with its own settings no longer follows the default until you reset it to the default.
help.searchSensitivity.extraction.title: Concept check
help.searchSensitivity.extraction.body: When LEAP extracts concepts from your material, it checks each concept against your material. A stricter setting gives fewer but better-supported concepts. Students only see concepts that pass this check.
help.chatInstructions.perCourse.title: Instructions per course
help.chatInstructions.perCourse.body: Give one course its own instructions for the chat or “I explain”, for example a different tone or subject-specific guidance. Courses without their own instructions use the general instructions above.
help.projects.submissions.title: Submitting project products
help.projects.submissions.body: When submission is on (via Edit), each group can submit one file; a new upload replaces the previous one. Here you see and download all submissions. An evaluator persona can give feedback on them.
help.projects.docs.title: Project documents
help.projects.docs.body: Material for this project, such as the assignment, sources or a dataset. The eye icon decides whether students see it. Personas use text files as background; students can only download datasets.
help.personas.consultationLimits.title: Number of conversations
help.personas.consultationLimits.body: How often a group may consult this persona. One consultation is one whole conversation. A quiet conversation can be closed automatically after a number of hours, so continuing counts as a new one. Leave empty for no limit.
help.personas.hiddenRubric.title: Hidden rubric
help.personas.hiddenRubric.body: The assessment criteria this evaluator uses to look at submitted work. Students do not see the rubric unless you make it visible. This lets you assess without students writing towards the criteria.
help.courses.cueRange.title: Relationship range
help.courses.cueRange.body: After each conversation a persona may adjust its relationship with the group slightly, within this range (1–5). A higher number means personas change their attitude faster based on how the group behaves.

help.personas.avatar.body: Every persona automatically gets a robot. Choose another style here, browse each feature with the arrows or click "Surprise me". Students see this face next to the name and beside every answer in the chat.
